title: Stakes set the reliability a score needs
statement: Let a score drive only the decisions its reliability supports, holding high-stakes decisions about one student to a stricter bar than screening or instructional ones.
example: One testing package set reliability of 0.90 for high-stakes decisions about one student and 0.85 for screening and instructional ones.
detail: A reading assessment's simulation evidence sets its reliability benchmarks at 0.90 for high-stakes interpretation of an individual score and 0.85 for screening and instructional decisions, attributing both to the professional testing standards. It reads its simulated core-range reliability of 0.928 as well above the 0.85 minimum for screening, and defines the range it measures reliably as the abilities where reliability reaches 0.85.
against: The cut-offs are the package's attribution to the 2014 testing standards, given with no page, DOI or URL, and were not checked against that source here.

evidence.quote: Statistical basis: reliability ≥ 0.90 is the standard for high-stakes individual score interpretation; ≥ 0.85 is acceptable for screening and instructional decision-making [AERA-2014].
well above the minimum acceptable threshold of 0.85 for screening decisions [AERA-2014]
Reliable range defined as: reliability ≥ 0.85 at that theta level
